Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
So at our tournament the other night, there was a question if Oubliette's
superior ability (burn a blood after the S:CE) worked if combat ended at
long range (i.e. I attck you, I manuver to long, you Oubliette at superior).

We were unsure, based on knowing that Catatonic Fear's superior damage was
updated at some point to only work if range was close whan combat ended, so
the general consensus among the cadre of judges was that it only worked at
close range, due to the Catatonic Fear precident.

I just went to look and make sure, and apparently, Oubliette has no such
limitation. Which is fine, but I'm wondering why?

Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:

news:BE198E24.1CBD0%pd...@lightlink.com...

> LSJ wrote:
>
> > The shadows have a longer reach.
>
> Sounds good to me.

Or, more card game specifically, Catatonic Fear has its "close range only"
enshrined in its current (CE) printing. Since Oubliette has no such
restriction (nor do some other strike: combat ends side effects), it works
no matter what the range during combat was.
